statement: For every integer n >= 1 and every real alpha with 0 <= alpha < 1, the frozen ladder problem has an attained infimum. Its value is [1-(n+1)alpha^2]/[2(n+1)(1-alpha)] when 0 <= alpha <= 1/(n+1), and (1-alpha)/(2n) when 1/(n+1) <= alpha < 1. The attaining ladder is unique: R_i=i/[(n+1)(1-alpha)] in the first regime and R_i=i/n in the second, for 1 <= i <= n; the descriptions coincide at alpha=1/(n+1). This includes the exact objective derivation, all equality and attainment cases under the strict ladder inequalities, direct n=1 and n=2 verification, alpha=0, transition continuity, and the limit alpha approaching 1. The claim is only for the frozen uniform-plus-endpoint-atom law and not for general atomic bandwidth distributions.
contribution: A complete finite-n solution of the frozen one-endpoint-atom specialization, extending the cited atom-free uniform calculation by identifying the boundary active-set transition and every optimizer. The proof is elementary and exact. No novelty or priority claim is made, and the cited source's broader atomic-distribution problem is not claimed solved.
